why: The durable protocol itself is pinned by conformance/durable-v1/scenarios.json, which every endpoint and client runs. These are the behaviours of the *reference worker* that sits above it - envelope handling, metric normalisation, receipt canonicalisation, lease discipline - which each binding implements in its own language and therefore cannot share a test for. Listing them here is what makes parity checkable: each binding's suite claims an id per test and fails when an id it does not cover appears, so a behaviour added to one binding cannot be quietly missing from the other.

behaviours.behaviour: An engine envelope payload yields the genome source for the evaluator; a raw payload passes through unchanged.
behaviours.why: A binding that mishandles the envelope evaluates the wrong text and still reports a completed receipt.

behaviours.behaviour: A metric that is not a finite scalar (an array, a NaN or infinity, an out-of-range integer) is recorded as text, never turned into a failure.
behaviours.why: Recording it as a failure throws away a real evaluation; emitting it as a JSON number produces a receipt the other binding cannot read.

behaviours.behaviour: A receipt payload is sorted-key JSON with no non-finite numbers, so two workers' receipts for the same evaluation compare as bytes.
behaviours.why: Byte-comparable receipts are what let a campaign reconcile two workers; key order alone would break that.

behaviours.behaviour: Every claimed lease is committed exactly once, and an evaluator that raises becomes a failed receipt rather than a crashed worker.
behaviours.why: A lease committed twice or not at all strands work the host is still waiting on.

behaviours.behaviour: An evaluation-result object (not a plain mapping) keeps its metrics and artifacts, and the lease limit bounds the serve loop.
behaviours.why: Upstream evaluators return result objects; dropping their artifacts loses the evidence a run is judged on.

behaviours.behaviour: An evaluator module with no `evaluate` is refused when it is loaded, before any lease is claimed.
behaviours.why: Refusing at the first lease instead would claim work the worker can never commit.

behaviours.behaviour: An envelope that will not parse, and an evaluator that returns nothing, each produce a failed receipt.
behaviours.why: Both are the worker's fault to report, not the host's to time out.

behaviours.behaviour: A commit the host refuses is propagated; the worker never re-runs the evaluator to retry it.
behaviours.why: Re-running charges the evaluation twice and can change the answer a receipt already claimed.

behaviours.behaviour: A lease enqueued by the engine bridge is evaluated as its genome source, end to end against the real host.
behaviours.why: This is the only case that proves the binding and the host agree about what a lease contains.
